subject: Geopolitics
title: The New START and Nuclear Limits
description: A short lesson to help you apply The New START and Nuclear Limits.

hook.text: New START limits the US and Russia to 1,550 deployed nuclear warheads each. It's the last nuclear arms treaty standing.

buildup.text: Signed in 2010, it included on-site inspections and data exchanges. Transparency reduced miscalculation risk.

discovery.text: Arms limits don't eliminate weapons. They create predictability. Each side knows what the other has.

twist.text: Russia suspended participation in 2023. With no inspections, neither side can verify the other's compliance.

climax.text: If New START dies with no replacement the world enters an unconstrained nuclear era for the first time since 1972.

punchline.text: The treaty holding back the arms race is hanging by a thread.

quiz.question: What makes New START strategically important?
options: It eliminates all nuclear weapons within 10 years
It creates predictability through warhead limits and inspections
It includes China as a third party to negotiations
